english: A rod you built yourself, with a sturdy pole, wrapped guides and a crude reel. Tap primary for a short cast, or hold it to cast farther. Bait and lures go in the Tackle panel under Modify; hold Reload to swap. When the float goes under, press primary, then hold to reel and ease off when the fish runs. Secondary reels the line back in.
Live bait. Bluegill, perch, bass and trout love them. One is used each time a fish takes the bait.
A 2.1 m carbon spinning rod with a smooth 5.2:1 reel. Casts further and keeps a bigger fish under control.
Chopped meat or fish scraps. Draws catfish, pike, sturgeon, turtles and anything that eats meat.
Cornmeal kneaded with river water. Carp love it, shrimp and beavers too.
Rotten meat laced with something that glows. Bites come faster at night and the wasteland's mutations go for it.

A wire cage for catching small water creatures. Place it in water at least one block deep and add bait to its bait slot. It catches nothing without bait. Every 4 hours, it has about a 60% chance of a catch, slightly higher with bait the animal prefers. Each catch uses one bait. It holds up to 6 catches (10 with a Bigger Cage) and keeps working for up to 48 hours while you are away. Depending on the water, it can catch crayfish, crabs, shrimp, eels, turtles and small panfish such as bluegill and perch. Traps in the same water share the available catches, and zombies can break them. Open the trap to see its next check, what lives in the water and which bait works best. It also has three slots for trap mods.
Fish fillets charred over an open fire. It'll keep you going.
Fish fillets grilled over the fire. Simple and good.
Crayfish tails, crab and shrimp boiled in clean water.
Clams, mussels and snails steamed open in a pot.
Frog legs fried crisp in animal fat.
A dark, rich soup of turtle meat, potato and corn.
Fish, potato and corn simmered in a pot.
Clams and mussels in a thick potato broth.
A pot of crawfish, corn and potatoes. Messy, filling, worth it.
Fried fish and potatoes, cooked in animal fat.
A small, round sunfish with an orange belly. Bites readily on worms near weeds and logs.
A striped yellow perch from open lake water. Two or three bobs, then a steady dip.
A heavy bronze carp from shallow, murky water. Slow to bite, slower to tire.
A largemouth bass. Hits hard near cover and jumps when hooked.
A rainbow trout from cold, clear water. Fast runs and the odd leap.
A channel catfish from deep holes. Feeds at night and pulls like a mule.
A longnose gar, armoured and toothy. Thrashes at the surface and can bite through a plain line.
A northern pike from big lakes. Short, explosive runs and a mouth full of teeth.
A lake sturgeon, an armoured giant from the deepest water. Its roe sells for a fortune.
A carp gone wrong in wasteland water: lumpy, glowing and angry. Cook it before you eat it.
An American eel, long and slick. Eels run up rivers into lakes and feed at night on the bottom.
A snapping turtle from a big lake: a slow, heavy pull and a beak that takes fingers.
A spiny softshell turtle: a flat leathery shell and a snout like a snorkel. It buries itself in soft, warm mud.
A red swamp crayfish (crawfish, crawdad): warm, muddy water. Six of them clean down to a portion of tail meat.
A signal crayfish (crawfish, crawdad) from cool, rocky water, with a pale patch at each claw joint. Four make a portion.
A freshwater crab that lives under rocks along warm, shaded banks. Three make a portion of crab meat.
Freshwater shrimp from weedy water. Ten make a portion, or put one on a hook: pike and bass love them.
A small ridged clam gathered from sandy beds in the shallows. Eight make a portion.
A big, thin-shelled lake mussel gathered from stable bottoms. Two make a portion.
A large pond snail from weedy shallows. Five make a portion, or use them as bait in a trap or on a hook.
A big bullfrog caught at the water's edge after dark. Its legs are good eating.
A green frog from cool pond edges, with a bright green upper lip. Three make a portion of frog legs.
A raw fish fillet. Cook it, or risk eating it raw.

A raw fillet from a mutant carp, faintly glowing. Eaten raw, it carries twice the usual risk of food poisoning. Cooking makes it safe: Charred Fish, Grilled Fish, Fish Stew and Fish Tacos can all be cooked from it.
Heads, tails and guts. Makes good cut bait.
Raw crayfish tails, crab and snail meat. Boil it before you eat it.
Glowing slime from the wasteland's water. Mixed into glow bait.
Sturgeon eggs. Traders pay a fortune for them.
Raw clam, mussel and snail meat. Steam or boil it before you eat it.
Raw frog legs. Fry them; they taste like you'd expect.
Raw turtle meat, dark and rich. Best in a soup.
Capstone: 5 Glow Bait, The Patient Angler vol. 7
Capstone: Crankbait, Wire Leader, 2 Angler's Monthly

Every fishing trip starts with a rod. The [DECEA3]Standard Fishing Rod[-] is known from the start and is crafted in your backpack.\n\nHold it near water: a small marker shows where the float will land, and the line under the crosshair gives the depth, or the reason a cast won't work.
Catch your first fish on a rod.

You need bait or a lure to cast. [DECEA3]Earthworms[-] turn up when you dig soil, about one block in twenty.\n\nTap [action:local:Primary] for a short cast, or hold it to cast farther. When the float goes under, strike with [action:local:Primary]. Hold it to reel, and let go to ease off when the line is in the red. Hold [action:permanent:Reload][action:local:Reload] with the rod out to swap bait.
[DECEA3]Earthworms[-] turn up when you dig dirt, forest ground or grass, about one block in twenty. A shovel is quickest.\n\nEvery fish will take them as bait.
Any fish caught on a rod counts, kept or released. Water thins out as you keep fish from it, so if bites slow down, move farther along a big lake or try different water.
Open a fish in your backpack and press [DECEA3]Fillet[-]. You'll get [DECEA3]Raw Fish Fillet[-], fish scraps for cut bait and, from fish over 1 kg, a bone. One press fillets the whole stack.
Catch a bluegill, a perch and a carp.

Three common fish. [DECEA3]Bluegill[-] prefer pine and burnt forest water, [DECEA3]perch[-] pine and snow, and [DECEA3]carp[-] desert, burnt forest and wasteland. Each can still turn up outside its usual waters, just less often. Carp love dough bait.
Catch a fish on earthworms, one on cut bait and one on dough bait.

[DECEA3]Cut Bait[-] unlocks at Fishing 3 (raw meat or fish scraps), and [DECEA3]Dough Bait[-] at Fishing 5 (cornmeal and murky water). Catfish and large predators prefer cut bait; carp prefer dough.\n\nHold [action:permanent:Reload][action:local:Reload] with the rod out to swap what's on the hook.
Catch a fish on cut bait
Catch a fish on dough bait
Cook Charred Fish or Grilled Fish and eat it.
[DECEA3]Charred Fish[-] needs only a campfire and three fillets. [DECEA3]Grilled Fish[-] needs a cooking grill and Cooking 6, and provides more food.
Reach Fishing skill 5 by reading Angler's Monthly.
[DECEA3]Angler's Monthly[-] raises the Fishing crafting skill. Higher skill unlocks better rod quality, bait, tackle and the Fishing Trap.
Catch 3 different fish, fillet 5 and cook 3 Charred or Grilled Fish.
Put what you've learned in the first chapter to use: catch a few kinds of fish, fillet them and cook them.
Catch a fish at dawn, between 05:00 and 08:00.
Bites come faster at dawn and dusk, when bass are hungriest. Dawn is 05:00-08:00, day 08:00-17:00, dusk 17:00-20:00 and night 22:00-04:00 on the game clock.
Catch a fish at night, between 22:00 and 04:00.

Catfish and eels feed at night, and sturgeon feed more at night than during the day. [DECEA3]Glow Bait[-] brings bites much faster in the dark. Dawn is 05:00-08:00, day 08:00-17:00, dusk 17:00-20:00 and night 22:00-04:00 on the game clock.
Bites come faster in the rain. If rain can never fall in this world's waters (some weather mods disable it), fish caught at dawn or dusk count instead. The tracker will show the change.
Catch fish at dawn or dusk (no rain in this world)
Catch 10 fish at dawn or dusk.
Bites come fastest at dawn (05:00-08:00) and dusk (17:00-20:00).
Catch fish at dawn or dusk
Night is 22:00-04:00. Bring a light for the walk home and stay alert. The world doesn't stop while you fish.
Catch a fish in small water and another in a big lake.

A big lake is a connected stretch of water with about 500 square metres of surface or more. Pike and sturgeon only live in big lakes. If your world has no big lake, any natural water counts for the second catch.
Catch a fish in small water
Catch a fish in a big lake
Catch a fish in natural water (no big lake in this world)
Catch a bass, a trout and a catfish.
[DECEA3]Bass[-] bite best at dawn and dusk, [DECEA3]trout[-] live in cool pine and snow water, and [DECEA3]catfish[-] feed at night on cut bait.
Catch a fish in water you built.
Dig a pond and fill it, or fish from a pier you built. A cast needs 2 blocks of water beneath the float, and larger waters hold more kinds of fish. A pond gets its fish from the biome it's in.
Catch a fish in water you built
Catch a fish in every biome of your world that has fishable water.

Only biomes with natural water 2 or more blocks deep count. The list is read when your world loads, so it matches your map. The tracker shows which biomes remain. A fish caught in water you built counts for the biome it's in. If your world has no natural water or no readable water map, any 3 biomes count.
Catch a fish in each biome with water ({0})
Catch a fish in 3 different biomes
Catch a fish at dawn, by day, at dusk, at night and in the rain.

Dawn is 05:00-08:00, day 08:00-17:00, dusk 17:00-20:00 and night 22:00-04:00. A catch in the rain counts for both rain and its time of day. If rain can never fall in this world's waters, any 4 of the 5 are enough.
5000 XP, 5 Glow Bait, The Patient Angler vol. 7
Catch a fish at each time ({0})
A [DECEA3]Spinner[-] unlocks at Fishing 11. Lures are never used up. Cast, then reel back steadily. You only lose one when the line snaps.
Fit a rod mod to a fishing rod.
Rod mods fit into the rod's mod slots like weapon mods. The [DECEA3]Cork Grip Wrap[-] (Fishing 8) is the first. A Standard rod has one slot at quality 1 and 2, and two from quality 3.
Carp take [DECEA3]Dough Bait[-] three times as eagerly as anything else. Their home is warm, slow water in the desert, burnt forest or wasteland.
A steady, medium retrieve works best with a spinner. Bass, perch and trout chase it.
Catch 10 fish on glow bait at night.
[DECEA3]Glow Bait[-] unlocks at Fishing 25. At night, it brings bites much faster, and mutant carp take it twice as often.
Catch fish on glow bait at night
Catch a fish on each lure: spinner, jig, crankbait and trout fly.

Spinner (Fishing 11): reel steadily. Jig (18): lift, pause, let it sink. Crankbait (24): reel faster to dive deeper. Trout fly (34): short twitches at the surface. The right retrieve triggers a cue and raises the chance of a strike.
Catch a fish on a spinner
Catch a fish on a jig
Catch a fish on a crankbait
Catch a fish on a trout fly
Fit a line mod and a rig mod to the same rod.
Line mods: Braided Line, Fluorocarbon Line, Wire Leader. Rig mods: Slip Float, Bottom Sinker. You can't fit two mods of the same type, and you need a rod with two mod slots.
Fit a line mod and a rig mod to one rod
Land a pike, a gar or a mutant carp with a Wire Leader fitted.
Toothy fish shake their heads during runs, causing tension spikes on a plain line. A [DECEA3]Wire Leader[-] (Fishing 28) prevents those spikes.
Land a toothy fish with a Wire Leader
Fishing 30 unlocks the [DECEA3]Precision Fishing Rod[-]: longer casts, a stronger line and a faster reel.
Craft a Precision Fishing Rod, fit 2 mods to it and land a fish with it.
The Precision rod is crafted at a workbench. It has two mod slots from quality 1.
Fit 2 mods to a Precision Fishing Rod
Land a fish with the Precision rod
The [DECEA3]Fishing Trap[-] is crafted at a workbench from Fishing 6. Place it in water at least one block deep.
Catch a frog at night, between 22:00 and 04:00.

Frogs stay near the edges of ponds and lakes from dusk until dawn, with more out in the rain. When one notices you (5 metres standing, 2.5 metres crouched), it freezes briefly before jumping in. Press [action:local:Activate] while it's frozen and within reach. Crouching improves your chance; running or a light sends it off at once.
Empty a Fishing Trap with a catch in it 5 times.
Put bait in the trap's [DECEA3]bait slot[-]. Every 4 in-game hours, the trap has a chance to catch something. Each catch uses one bait. Take everything the trap caught to count a haul.
Empty a trap with a catch in it
[DECEA3]Red swamp crayfish[-] live in warm, murky shallows, while [DECEA3]signal crayfish[-] prefer cool, rocky water. Earthworms attract both. Each trap catch contains several.
Gather from clam beds, mussel beds or snail patches 10 times.
Beds sit on the bottom in shallow water, one or two blocks deep, near shore. Wade in and press [action:local:Activate]. Each bed gives three gathers, then regrows over 3 in-game days.
Trap a spiny softshell and land a snapping turtle on a rod.
Softshells live in warm water with soft bottoms and like cut bait. Snapping turtles take cut bait on a rod, with a slow, heavy pull. Only juvenile snapping turtles fit in a trap.
Land a snapping turtle on a rod
Land a snapping turtle over 8 kg and an eel on a rod.
Anything weighing 8 kg or more is pulled onto the bank instead of swung in. Eels feed on cut bait at night and twist as they fight.
Land a snapping turtle over 8 kg
Land an eel on a rod
Empty a trap holding all 6 catches.

A trap holds six catches, then stops until you empty it. It only catches with bait in the bait slot and water around it. Traps in the same small pond share its fish. Look at a trap to check its state.
Catch, trap or gather every lake animal that isn't a fish.

Snapping turtle, spiny softshell, red swamp crayfish, signal crayfish, crab, freshwater shrimp, clam, mussel, mystery snail, bullfrog and green frog. Each can appear in any biome with water, but is most common in its own. Previous catches count.
Empty 3 different traps with a catch in one in-game day, gather from each kind of bed, and catch a frog with a Dip Net swing.

A [DECEA3]Dip Net[-] (Fishing 4, crafted in your backpack) reaches about 3 m and catches more frogs than your hands. Hold it, aim at a frog, and press [action:local:Primary] to swing. Grabbing one with [action:local:Activate][action:permanent:Activate] doesn't count.
Empty different traps in one day
Catch a frog with a Dip Net swing
Pike live in big lakes at least 4 blocks deep, especially in snow and pine forest water. They take jigs, crankbaits and cut bait. If your world has no big lake, a gar counts instead.
Catch a gar (no big lake in this world)
Gar swim near the surface of water 4 or more blocks deep, mostly by day in the desert and burnt forest. Crankbait and cut bait work.
Press [action:local:Secondary] while the catch card is visible to release the fish. You get a quarter of the XP, the spot doesn't thin out, and the fish still counts for your records and challenges.
Gar, pike, sturgeon and mutant carp are the rare fish. Fish from stocked ponds don't count.
A long haul. Every fish caught on a rod counts, kept or released.
Catch a wild sturgeon and a wild mutant carp.

Sturgeon need a big lake at least 6 blocks deep and bite best at night on cut bait or a bottom rig. Mutant carp need water at least 4 blocks deep in the wasteland or within 500 metres of it. Without a deep big lake in your world, any wild trophy fish counts for the sturgeon; without deep wasteland water, the mutant carp requirement is dropped.
Catch a wild trophy fish (no deep lake in this world)
Catch wild trophy-size fish of 3 different species.
A trophy is a catch in the top 5% of its species' weight range; the catch card shows the badge. Fish from a stocked pond are never trophies.
Land a wild fish weighing more than 20 kg.
Only a sturgeon grows past 20 kg. If your world has no big lake at least 6 blocks deep, a wild fish over 6.5 kg counts instead.
Land a wild fish over 20 kg
Land a wild fish over 6.5 kg (no deep lake in this world)
Catch every fish species at least once.
Bluegill, perch, carp, bass, trout, catfish, gar, pike, sturgeon, mutant carp and eel. Any method and any water count, a pond fish included, and fish you caught before count too.
Catch a wild pike, gar, sturgeon and mutant carp within 7 in-game days.

They live in different waters, so plan the trip. Only the rare fish your world can hold are asked for: pike need a big lake 4 blocks deep, sturgeon a big lake 6 deep, gar water 4 deep, mutant carp wasteland water 4 deep. The tracker lists the ones still to catch.
5000 XP, Crankbait, Wire Leader, 2 Angler's Monthly
Catch each rare fish within 7 days ({0})
Accept a fishing job from a trader.
Ask any trader [DECEA3]Got any fishing work?[-] to open the Fishing Jobs board. Each trader offers three jobs a day; you can hold two.
A fresh order asks for a few fish of one kind. Commodity jobs accept fish from a stocked pond.
Turn finished jobs in at any trader's board. Every job adds to your Angler standing.
Release 10 fingerlings into a stocked pond.
Build water at least 7 by 7 and 3 deep, register it with a [DECEA3]Pond Marker[-] (Fishing 31) and release fingerlings bought from traders. A new pond takes 3 in-game days to settle.
Higher standing unlocks harder jobs and better pay.
Finish a Fresh order, a Biome run and a Night shift.
Biome runs open at standing 2 and night shifts at standing 3. Wild jobs need wild fish.
Read 3 different volumes of The Patient Angler.
The seven volumes of [DECEA3]The Patient Angler[-] each teach one technique. They turn up as loot and, rarely, at traders.
Catch a fish from a stocked pond.
A stocked pond refills slowly, about one fish an hour up to what it can hold. Pond fish are marked farmed.
Catch a fish from a stocked pond
Standing grows with every finished job. The top rank brings legend hunts and the best pay.
Read all 7 volumes of The Patient Angler and finish the capstones of chapters 1 to 5.
Reading the whole series also earns the Master Angler bonus: rare fish bite twice as often and every catch rolls heavier.
10000 XP, Spinner, Jig, Crankbait, Trout Fly
[DECEA3]Pan-Fried Fish[-] is the first fish dish Culinary Hearth teaches: fillets fried in fat with herbs and lemon.
Pick fish on the meat row of any meal, like Tacos or Ramen.
Twelve of Culinary Hearth's any-meat meals take fish. Pick it on the meat row of the recipe and cook it.
Any dish made with fish counts, from Charred Fish to a Sashimi Plate.
[DECEA3]Smoked Fish[-] is salted and smoked, and keeps for a long trip.
Every fish filleted in the backpack counts.
Cook Fish and Chips and Beer-Battered Fish.
Two fried classics from Culinary Hearth.
Make Nigiri, a Fish and Rice Bowl and a Poke Bowl.
Raw and seared fish over rice.
Make a Fish and Rice Bowl
Fish meals help you swim faster and hold your breath longer.
Cook fish in all 12 any-meat meals.
Grilled Plate, Meat Sandwich, Skewers, Noodle Soup, Burger, Tacos, Corn Chowder, Meat Pie, Fried Rice, Fried Cutlet, Ramen and Breakfast Burrito, each made with fish.

Hold: hold primary to reel and let go to ease off. Toggle: tap primary to start reeling and tap again to ease off. Applies immediately.

Size of the bite ring around the crosshair when a fish bites. 100% is the standard size.

Junk is old scrap that snags the hook instead of a fish: scrap metal, cloth, plastic, an empty can or occasionally a lost lure. It comes in with a short drag, not a fight, and uses no bait. The host or server sets this for everyone.

The chance that a bite on a rod brings up junk instead of an animal. The server rolls it once per bite.

Off: no strongboxes on the line or in Fishing Traps.

How often a Fishing Trap checks for a catch, whether trap mods work, and whether it can bring up junk or treasure instead. Trap salvage is off by default: traps keep working while you're away, so even small chances add up over a long game. The host or server sets these for everyone.
Off: traps catch only animals. Junk only: a trap catch can be junk. Junk and treasure: it can also be a strongbox.

Controls what the Dip Net can do and how much traps and scoops bring up. The host or server sets these for everyone.
On: the Dip Net scoops shallow water near the bank for shrimp, crayfish and small panfish. Off: it only swings at frogs.
Scales how many crayfish, shrimp, crabs and similar animals are brought up by each trap catch or scoop. A fish is always one fish. 1x by default.
Controls which junk and treasure can be caught. An item only comes up when its group and individual switches are both on. If nothing in a group is on, the catch is an animal instead.

Bait and lures go on the rod, like ammo in a gun. The rod's Tackle panel under Modify has a Bait slot and a Lure slot. A loaded lure is cast instead of bait. A landed catch appears on the card at the right. Press [action:local:Secondary] while it's showing to release it. You get a quarter of the XP, the water doesn't thin, and it still counts in your journal. Do anything else and it goes into your pack.

Place a trap in water and put bait in its bait slot. Every 4 in-game hours, it gets one chance to catch something. Each catch uses one bait. A trap holds six catches. Traps in the same stretch of water share what's available.

Clam beds, mussel beds and snail patches grow on the bottom of shallow water near the shore. Stand in or beside the water and press [action:local:Activate][action:permanent:Activate] to gather. Each bed gives 3 gathers, then replenishes after 3 days.

Frogs appear along the banks at dusk and at night, with more appearing in the rain. When a frog notices you, it freezes briefly before jumping into the water. Move closer while it freezes and press [action:local:Activate][action:permanent:Activate] to grab it, or hold a Dip Net and press [action:local:Primary] to swing from farther away. Running or using a light scares it off immediately. Crouching improves your chance of catching it, and the net improves it further. The net can also scoop shallow water near the bank for shrimp, crayfish and small panfish. Repeatedly scooping the same spot reduces catches for a couple of hours.

Keeping fish from the same water thins the population, slowing bites until it recovers over a few hours. Ponds and small lakes thin out as a whole; big lakes thin one stretch at a time. Nearby gunshots, explosions and swimming spook fish for a minute. Released fish don't thin the water.
